steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since your filler with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still happy with how it looks, it's starting to soften, or it's pretty much gone. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Still Happy With It
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes treatment with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still happy with the results.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Starting to Soften
steps.content:
That happens, {{contact_first_name}}. Filler softens over time, and the face keeps changing on its own. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were happy with how it turned out. What kept you from coming back in?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Pretty Much Gone
steps.content:
I'm sorry to hear that, {{contact_first_name}}. Filler does soften and wear off over time. It's not anything you did wrong. Your notes say you were happy with the result. Was it cost, timing, or something else that kept you from coming back?

(Let them answer. Stay warm. Do not book yet.)

steps.title: Ask Permission for the Questions
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask you a few quick questions about anything else you've noticed?

(Wait for the yes. It's their file, so almost everyone says yes.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said the result has softened. We'll come back to that. First, can I ask you a few quick questions so your file is up to date?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name. You'll recap them in a moment.)

First, your lips. Have they thinned out again, or are they still where you want them?

How about your cheeks, any volume loss making them look flatter than they used to?

What about the smile lines, the ones that run from your nose to the corners of your mouth?

Any hollows under your eyes that make you look tired when you're not?

How about your jawline and chin, anything there you'd like more defined?

Any little lines around your mouth, the kind lipstick settles into?

How about the lines on your forehead or between your brows?

And the skin itself, has it been looking rough or dull lately?

Any sun spots or uneven tone showing up?

Last one. Any loosening or sagging, especially along the jaw or neck?

(Recap what you wrote down, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(They already named one area. Write down every area they name, including that one.)

First, your lips. Have they thinned out again, or are they still where you want them?

How about your cheeks, any volume loss making them look flatter than they used to?

What about the smile lines, the ones that run from your nose to the corners of your mouth?

Any hollows under your eyes that make you look tired when you're not?

How about your jawline and chin, anything there you'd like more defined?

Any little lines around your mouth, the kind lipstick settles into?

How about the lines on your forehead or between your brows?

And the skin itself, has it been looking rough or dull lately?

Any sun spots or uneven tone showing up?

Last one. Any loosening or sagging, especially along the jaw or neck?

(Recap everything, including what they mentioned at the start, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, between what you mentioned earlier and these, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Pause after each and let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a few weeks, or more like months?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice now and then, or every time you look in the mirror?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with photos, going out, or feeling put together?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Read back their three answers: how long, how often, what it gets in the way of.)

So it's been on your mind a while, and you notice it most times you look in the mirror. At its worst it gets in the way of what you mentioned. Did I get that right?

(Say what they named: photos, going out, or feeling put together. Let them answer. If they correct you, take the correction and move on.)

And it sounds like you'd really like to look in the mirror and feel good about it again. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why Did They Stop?
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still happy with it.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Listen all the way through. Do not argue with it.)

Filler softens slowly, so most people don't notice it going until it's gone. A check-in now and then keeps the look you like. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in for a check-in so you keep the look you have. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “It wore off, so what’s the point?”
steps.content:
That's fair. Filler is meant to soften over time, and the face keeps changing on its own. That's why a check-in makes sense, so we can see where things are now and what would help.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: “I didn’t see enough of a difference”
steps.content:
I appreciate you telling me. That's the kind of thing we'd want to talk through in person. That way {{provider_name}} can hear what you were hoping for and see what would get you closer.

(Do not promise results on the call.)

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m nervous about looking overdone”
steps.content:
That's a common worry, and it's a good one to say out loud. Most people want to look rested, not different. Coming in is where you get to say exactly that, and we listen.

(Do not promise a look on the call.)

Would it help to come in and talk it through first?

steps.title: Objection: “I went somewhere else”
steps.content:
That's okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm glad you kept it up. Your whole history is here, including what was done and where. We can pick up right where you left off.

(Stay easy. Do not ask why they left.)

Would you be open to coming back in?

steps.title: If They Say: “I was happy with my results”
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}, and that's the best reason there is. When you like what you see, coming back stops feeling urgent. The thing with filler is that it softens so slowly you don't notice it going. Does that make sense?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule so you keep the look you like. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: Cost or Budget
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. A check-in is just a look. You're not committing to anything. It's one visit so we can see how everything is holding.

Does that seem fair?

(Let them answer.)

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “Life got busy”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and this kind of thing gets pushed down the list. It happens to everyone. A check-in visit is quick, and we can find a time that works around your schedule.

Would that work?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule at a time that's easy for you. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: “I’ll come back when it wears off”
steps.content:
That's a fair way to think about it, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd share is that filler goes slowly. By the time you notice it's gone, it's been going for a while. It's easier to keep the look you have than to start over.

Does that sound right?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule before it's gone. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: If They Say: They Moved or Tried Another Provider
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're still in the area, we'd love to see you again. Your whole history is in your file, so we can pick up right where you left off.

Would that be okay?

(Let them answer.)

Was there anything else holding you back, or was that pretty much it?

(If they raise another reason, go back and tap the button for it. If that was it, continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you back on the schedule. Does that sound reasonable?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people just want to be sure it's right for them.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. You'd see what's possible and what it would involve, and then you decide with real answers. No pressure either way.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't show you what's possible for you specifically. That's what a quick visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Does that work for you?
